requirements.subject: ent:start-component-operation
requirements.canonical: The start test component operation IS the operation used to associate a test behaviour with a test component, which then executes that behaviour.
requirements.original: The start operation is used to associate a test behaviour to a test component, which is then being executed by that test component.

requirements.subject: ent:start-component-operation
requirements.canonical: The start test component operation has the syntax ObjectReference "." `start` "(" ( FunctionInstance | AltstepInstance ) ")".
requirements.original: ObjectReference "." start "(" ( FunctionInstance | AltstepInstance ) ")"

requirements.subject: ent:ptc
requirements.canonical: Once a PTC has been created, a behaviour SHALL be bound to the PTC and its execution SHALL be started.
requirements.original: Once a PTC has been created and connected, behaviour has to be bound to this PTC and the execution of its behaviour has to be started.

ambiguity.issue: 'created and connected' may be read as a precondition that the PTC is connected before start, or only as the typical order of operations. Connection is not required elsewhere in the standard, so the second reading is chosen.
readings: Once a PTC has been created, a behaviour SHALL be bound to it and started; connecting it before is optional.
A PTC SHALL be created and connected before a behaviour is bound to it and started.

requirements.subject: ent:start-component-operation
requirements.canonical: Binding a behaviour to a PTC and starting its execution IS done by the start test component operation.
requirements.original: This is done by using the start operation (as PTC creation does not start execution of the component behaviour).

requirements.subject: ent:create-operation
requirements.canonical: The creation of a PTC IS NOT the start of the execution of the component behaviour.
requirements.original: This is done by using the start operation (as PTC creation does not start execution of the component behaviour).

requirements.subject: ent:start-component-operation
requirements.canonical: The start test component operation SHALL bind the required behaviour to the test component.
requirements.original: The start operation shall bind the required behaviour to the test component.

requirements.subject: ent:test-behaviour
requirements.canonical: The behaviour started on a test component IS defined by reference to an already defined function or altstep.
requirements.original: This behaviour is defined by reference to an already defined function or altstep.

requirements.subject: ent:alive-type-ptc
requirements.canonical: An alive-type PTC MAY perform several behaviours in sequential order.
requirements.original: An alive-type PTC may perform several behaviours in sequential order.

requirements.subject: ent:start-component-operation
requirements.canonical: Starting a second behaviour on a non-alive PTC IS a test case error.
requirements.original: Starting a second behaviour on a non-alive PTC or starting a behaviour on a PTC that is still running results in a test case error.

requirements.subject: ent:start-component-operation
requirements.condition: the PTC is still running a behaviour
requirements.canonical: Starting a behaviour on a PTC that is still running IS a test case error.
requirements.original: Starting a second behaviour on a non-alive PTC or starting a behaviour on a PTC that is still running results in a test case error.

requirements.subject: ent:alive-type-ptc
requirements.condition: a previous behaviour has terminated on the alive-type PTC
requirements.canonical: A behaviour started on an alive-type PTC after termination of a previous behaviour IS executed with the variable values, timers, ports and local verdict as they were left after termination of the previous behaviour.
requirements.original: If a behaviour is started on an alive-type PTC after termination of a previous behaviour, it uses variable values, timers, ports, and the local verdict as they were left after termination of the previous behaviour.

requirements.subject: ent:test-behaviour
requirements.condition: a timer was started in the previous behaviour
requirements.canonical: If a timer was started in the previous behaviour of an alive-type PTC, the subsequent behaviour SHOULD be enabled to handle a possible timeout event.
requirements.original: In particular, if a timer was started in the previous behaviour, the subsequent behaviour should be enabled to handle a possible timeout event.

ambiguity.issue: It is unclear whether this is advice to the test writer (the subsequent behaviour should contain a timeout handler) or a requirement on the tool (pending timeout events of component timers are preserved and observable by the next behaviour).
readings: The test writer SHOULD write the subsequent behaviour of an alive-type PTC so that it handles a possible timeout of a timer started in the previous behaviour.
The TTCN-3 tool SHALL preserve timeout events of component timers started in a previous behaviour so that the subsequent behaviour can handle them.

requirements.subject: ent:default
requirements.canonical: Every active default IS deactivated when the behaviour of an alive-type PTC is stopped.
requirements.original: In contrast to that, all active defaults are deactivated when the behaviour of an alive-type PTC is stopped.

requirements.subject: ent:default
requirements.canonical: When a new behaviour is started on an alive-type PTC, a default IS NOT active.
requirements.original: This means no default is activated when a new behaviour is started on an alive-type PTC.

requirements.subject: ent:variable
requirements.canonical: The lifetime of a variable or timer IS bound to the scope in which it is declared.
requirements.original: NOTE 1: The lifetime of variables and timers is bound to the scope in which they are declared.

requirements.subject: ent:alive-type-ptc
requirements.canonical: When an alive-type component is stopped, only the component scope remains.
requirements.original: When an alive-type component is stopped, only the component scope is left.

ambiguity.issue: 'only the component scope is left' can mean that only the component scope remains, or that only the component scope is exited (left). The context (s016) supports the first reading.
readings: When an alive-type component is stopped, all scopes of the behaviour are exited and only the component scope remains.
When an alive-type component is stopped, only the component scope is exited.

requirements.subject: ent:test-behaviour
requirements.canonical: A behaviour with a corresponding runs on clause started on an alive-type PTC CAN access only the variable values and timers declared in the component type definition of that PTC from previous behaviours.
requirements.original: This means only variable values and timers declared in the component type definition of an alive-type PTC can be accessed by a behaviour with a corresponding runs on-clause that is started on an alive-type PTC.

requirements.subject: ent:actual-inout-parameter
requirements.canonical: In a start test component operation, an actual inout parameter IS passed to the started function by value, i.e. like an in parameter.
requirements.original: Actual inout parameters will be passed to the function by value, i.e. like in-parameters.

requirements.subject: ent:actual-out-parameter
requirements.condition: the formal parameter list of the function includes an out parameter
requirements.canonical: In a start test component operation, an actual out parameter MAY be omitted using the not-used symbol ("-").
requirements.original: If the function's formal parameter list includes any out parameter the actual parameter list may omit actual out parameters using the dash symbol ("-") or be omitted in the same manner as for actual in parameters with default values (see clause 5.4.2), i.e. they can be omitted in the list notation if all following actual parameters are also omitted and their assignment can be omitted altogether in assignment notation.

requirements.subject: ent:actual-out-parameter
requirements.canonical: In a start test component operation using list notation, an actual out parameter MAY be omitted if all following actual parameters are also omitted.
requirements.original: If the function's formal parameter list includes any out parameter the actual parameter list may omit actual out parameters using the dash symbol ("-") or be omitted in the same manner as for actual in parameters with default values (see clause 5.4.2), i.e. they can be omitted in the list notation if all following actual parameters are also omitted and their assignment can be omitted altogether in assignment notation.

requirements.subject: ent:actual-out-parameter
requirements.canonical: In a start test component operation using assignment notation, the assignment of an actual out parameter MAY be omitted altogether.
requirements.original: If the function's formal parameter list includes any out parameter the actual parameter list may omit actual out parameters using the dash symbol ("-") or be omitted in the same manner as for actual in parameters with default values (see clause 5.4.2), i.e. they can be omitted in the list notation if all following actual parameters are also omitted and their assignment can be omitted altogether in assignment notation.

requirements.subject: ent:actual-out-parameter
requirements.canonical: A variable given as an actual out parameter in a start test component operation IS left unchanged by the started behaviour, even if the behaviour changes the formal parameter during its execution.
requirements.original: If a variable is given as an actual out parameter, it will remain unchanged by the started behaviour, even if the behaviour changes the formal parameter during its execution.

requirements.subject: ent:return-value
requirements.canonical: A return value or out or inout parameter of a function invoked in a start test component operation IS NOT effective when the started test component terminates.
requirements.original: Possible return values of a function invoked in a start test component operation, i.e. templates denoted by return keyword or inout and out parameters, have no effect when the started test component terminates.

ambiguity.issue: Return values are called 'templates denoted by return keyword'; return values may be values or templates.

requirements.subject: ent:object-reference
requirements.canonical: The ObjectReference of a start test component operation SHALL be of component type.
requirements.original: a) The ObjectReference shall be of component type and shall not resolve to a template.

requirements.subject: ent:object-reference
requirements.canonical: The ObjectReference of a start test component operation SHALL NOT resolve to a template.
requirements.original: a) The ObjectReference shall be of component type and shall not resolve to a template.

requirements.subject: ent:runs-on-clause
requirements.canonical: A function or altstep invoked in a start test component operation SHALL have a runs on clause referencing a component type that is compatible with the test component referenced by the ObjectReference.
requirements.original: b) The function or altstep invoked in a start test component operation shall have a runs `on definition` referencing a component type that is compatible with the newly created component (see clause 6.3.2.7).

ambiguity.issue: 'runs on definition' should be 'runs on clause'; 'newly created component' should be the component addressed by the ObjectReference (which may be an alive-type PTC already used before).

improper_terms.proper: test component referenced by the ObjectReference

requirements.subject: ent:formal-parameter
requirements.canonical: Every formal parameter of a function or altstep invoked in a start test component operation SHALL be of a component data type.
requirements.original: c) All formal parameters of the function or altstep invoked in a start test component operation shall be of a component data type.

requirements.subject: ent:input-queue
requirements.canonical: When a test component starts execution, messages CAN already be waiting in the incoming queues of its in and inout ports, because these ports start listening when the component is created.
requirements.original: NOTE 2: As in and inout ports starts listening when the component is created, at the moment, when it starts execution there may be messages in the incoming queues of such ports already waiting to be processed.

ambiguity.issue: 'in and inout ports' is not a defined term; ports whose port type allows incoming communication is meant.

improper_terms.proper: ports whose port type declares in or inout messages

non_requirement.reason: rationale for separating create and start (to allow connection operations before running the component); no additional constraint
introductory sentence pointing to the general static rules in clauses 5, 21 and table 16; restrictions extracted from list items 21.3.2-s022..s024
